entries: **Twelve hidden Plush Pals: Bobo, Zippy, Twinkle, Tantan, Minto, Shandou, Nibo, Boqi, Zapi, Lei Tuan, WuQiu and Ban Ban.** They stay out of the normal line-up. When the panel loads there is a 1 in 10 chance one of them starts at the front, and each time the line rotates there is a 1 in 10 chance one of them hops in instead of the next regular pal. Each has ten poses: the usual five, plus waving to a neighbour, a big stretch, running when quota burns fast, a startled jump and a signature move it strikes now and then while waiting.

**Hidden Plush Pals unlock one a week, with a collector's book.** From Tuesday 1 December one hidden pal unlocks each week, in a fixed order; a pal that has not unlocked yet never appears. The first time you open the panel after a pal unlocks, it hops into the line, so a new pal is never left to chance; pals you have already met keep their rare random turns. The first time you meet one, a collectible card flips up and files itself into the book at the left end of the line. The book shows every hidden pal as a numbered card: found ones in colour, standing out of their frames and bobbing gently (hover to tilt), unlocked but not yet met as silhouettes, and the rest with their unlock date. Finding them all turns the book gold. The book scrolls when it is taller than the panel. With Reduce Motion on, the card and the tilt are skipped.

**Share a hidden pal's card (macOS).** When the card flips up it now grows to fill the panel and waits, with Share and Keep underneath. Share offers Post to Threads, Post to X, Copy Image, Save Image and More…. The picture is the card itself, with the usage link on its last line, on a 4:5 sheet. Threads and X open their post page with a line of text and the link filled in, and the picture is already on the clipboard, so ⌘V adds it. Save Image puts it in Downloads; More… opens the macOS share menu (Messages, AirDrop and other apps). Found pals in the book carry a share badge: click one to open its card again with Share and Close. Windows keeps the old card without sharing.

**Share today's usage as a card (macOS, every panel except World Cup).** A round share button sits at the right end of the footer's Today line, in the panel's own colours. It opens a Plush Pals card on every panel: today's date, a pal, today's token total, and a bar splitting today's tokens between services, with each service's tokens and share underneath. Services you did not use today are left out, and so are project names and costs. On the Plush Pals panel the pal comes from the line; elsewhere it is a random regular pal, never a hidden one. Share, the menu and the 4:5 picture work as they do for the hidden pals.
**Plush Pals opens on Windows and keeps your collection across launches on macOS and Windows.** The panel also remembers daily greetings and which weekly quota resets it has welcomed.

**The collector's book catches up on missed unlocks.** Each newly unlocked pal gets a turn, cards open one at a time, and the book's tooltip and card animations work at the panel's current language and scale.
**Today's share card includes Antigravity.** Sharing is available once today's totals are ready, and the card's date matches the day counted.
**Sharing confirms when an image is saved.** The card stays open and shows an error if the save fails. Confirmations for Threads and X stay centered and readable.

**Claude quota picks the newer eligible reading for the signed-in organization.** A newer Desktop reading can beat Claude Code's cached reading even when the two observations are less than a minute apart. usage can also read the matching Desktop HTTP cache without a history file when Claude Code identifies the organization.

**Claude quota from the desktop app works again on macOS.** Claude Desktop now keeps its HTTP cache in Chromium's simple-cache format, one file per response, and has stopped adding samples to `plan-usage-history.json`. usage only read the older block-file cache, so if you used Claude only in the desktop app the Claude card stayed at `--` or kept an old number. usage now also reads the simple-cache format. It takes the newest usage response Desktop stored in the last two hours, including ones with a query string such as `?via=plan`, and checks each one's checksums before using it. As before, it reads only local files, read-only, and sends nothing over the network.

**Quota used in the desktop app now shows up even after a terminal session.** Before, once a terminal Claude Code session had reported quota, usage kept showing that number and never looked at the desktop app, so usage in the app afterwards went missing (for example 37% in the menu bar while the app's own Usage page said 55%). Now, when the terminal reading is more than two minutes old and Claude Desktop has a newer one for the same organization you are signed in to in Claude Code, usage shows the Desktop number, in the app and in `usage status`. If the organization can't be matched, the terminal number stays.

**The Claude card explains what to do when it can't read quota from an installed Claude Desktop app.** It asks you to open Settings → Usage and wait a minute. If quota still doesn't show, it explains that a Desktop update may have changed how the app stores data and asks you to report it on GitHub.

**Antigravity's Gemini 4 Argon now reads the shared Gemini quota.** Antigravity CLI 1.5.16 dropped Argon's separate pool, so Argon shares the Gemini weekly and 5-hour limits. usage still looked for the old Argon pool, and Orchestrator models read the Claude / GPT pool. Now both read the Gemini pool in the status line, and the report counts Argon and Orchestrator conversations toward Gemini instead of dropping them. When the menu bar switches from Argon to Gemini, the burn rate starts over instead of showing a sudden jump.
